Often when I'm not paying attention to the sky I hear this weird sound that's definitely coming from jet planes, and it sounds like they're dropping into existence or something. It's usually when they're in the middle of the sky, not just appearing over the horizon. The only way I can describe it really is it starts at a higher pitch and drops quickly to a steady jet roar. Why?
Why do jet planes often have a weird dropping in sound when you first hear them in the sky?

I have no idea, so I'm just going to guess.

The Doppler effect. When they're far away, the sound has plenty of time to move out of the way of the vehicle, so they're not being compressed. But when they're overhead, all the air that is conducting the sound is still being pushed out of the way, compressing the soundwaves. The effect is brief, though, because the vehicle is moving so quickly.

Guessing also... If something changes slowly enough, it tends to go unnoticed. The plane's noise would gradually increase from when it was miles away until the point it is overhead. Possibly it is only when the plane is close enough that the noise reaches some given threshold, that the brain pays attention to it.
